source_text:
1.12 Πρὸς ὑποζυγίων φθοράν
Ἐμπόδιον στρατιώτῃ νοσήσας ἵππος καὶ ὑποζύγιον ἐν πολέμῳ ὁπλοφοροῦν καὶ τὰ
χρειώδη φέρων νωτοφόρος ὀρεύς· οἷς ἅπασι τὴν θεραπείαν τῶν τε ἄλλων καὶ
λοιμικῶν παθῶν τοιάνδε προσοιστέον. [Θεραπεία νοσούντων κτηνῶν]. Σελίνου
σπέρματος τρία ἡμίξεστα· κἀπίτριτον λινοσπέρμου· τήλεως δὲ τοῦ δευτέρου τὸ
διπλάσιον· ὀρόβου τε ἀλητοῦ τῆς τήλεως τετραπλάσιον· μέτρῳ μὲν ταῦτα· πάνακος
δὲ ῥίζης καὶ ἴρεως Ἰλλυρικῆς βράθυός τε τῆς ἀπὸ Σαβίνων πόας ἀνὰ ὀκτὼ καὶ
τεσσαράκοντα δραχμάς· καὶ τετραπλάσιον ἅμα τῶν τριῶν ἀξουγγίου παλαιοῦ
σταθμὸν τοῦ ἀνάλου. Τῶν δὲ προειρημένων ξηρῶν ἕκαστον ἰδίᾳ κόπτεται καὶ
σήθεται οἴνῳ τε παλαιῷ καὶ τῷ στῆρι παλύνεται, εἶτ' εἰς ἀρτίσκους ἀναπλασθέντα,
ἐν σκιᾷ ξηραίνεται· ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς χρείας, ὁπόσον καρύου μέγεθος βασιλικοῦ, (ὃ δὴ ἑπτὰ
γράμματα ἕλκει) σὺν μέλιτος κυάθοις τρισὶ λειοῦται, εἶτα οἴνῳ παλαιοτάτῳ καὶ
σπουδαιοτάτῳ ἀναλύεται· εἴη δὲ ξέστης εἷς· κἀπὶ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἑκάστου ἔτους τὸ
κτῆνος προσλαμβάνον οὐ πείσεται τὸ θανατήσιον τῶν κτηνῶν πάθος. Τοῖς δὲ
νοσοῦσιν, ἀντὶ τοῦ οἴνου, ὕδατι ἀναλύεται τῶν πρὸ τοῦ ἐπίσης εἰσηγησαμένων. Εἰ δὲ
πίτυι κἀκ τῆς νοσερᾶς συστάσεως ἀνάγκη γένοιτο χρῆσθαι, τῶν ἀρτίσκων ἀπουσίᾳ,
κολλύρας τρεῖς ἐγχυματίζειν οἴνῳ βρέχοντα, οἵῳ τρόπῳ καθ' αὑτὸ ἀξούγγιον ἐνιᾶσι
πολλοί. Οἷς δὲ λύκοι θηρῶνται ῥᾷστα, οἳ δ' οὕτως ἰῶνται τῶν προειρημένων παθῶν
τὰ ὑποζύγια· κρέως λυκείου τῶν σαρκῶν διαιροῦντες πλατείας σχελίδας, [καὶ]
ἰσχνὰς ἀφαυαίνουσιν ὑπὲρ καπνοῦ κρεμαννύντες, οἵας τῶν βοῶν ἡμεῖς. Χρὴ δ' ἐπὶ
τῆς χρείας ἑψεῖν τι τούτων ἔστ' ἂν συντακῇ, τῷ τε ὕδατι ἀνὰ ἡμίξεστον οἴνου τε καὶ
ἐλαίου μίξαντες, ἑκάστου ἔτους ἐγχυματίζειν. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ νεκροῦ κυνὸς ἤδη
σεσηπότος ἀποτμηθεῖσα κεφαλὴ νοσοῦντι τῷ ἵππῳ τὸ δεινὸν ἐκεῖνο πάθος
ὑπολύεται· ὃ δὲ τῇ τῆς ὀδμῆς ἀποφορᾷ συνεχεῖ καπνιζόμενος ἰαθήσεται. [Σύνθεσις
ποικιλωτέρα καὶ πολυϋλωτέρα.] Τὸ δὲ δὴ πολυϋλώτατον, οὗ πεῖραν ἔσχον αὐτός, ᾧ
χρῶνται Ῥωμαῖοι οἱ προήκοντες, μαθεῖν ἀναγκαῖον· ὅσον ὀκτὼ δραχμῶν ἀμώμου τε
τοῦ βοτρυΐτου καὶ πεπέριδος ἑκατέρας, μελαίνης τε καὶ λευκῆς <....> τὸ διπλάσιον· τριπλάσιον φύλλου πυρέθρου τε καὶ ἀριστολοχίας, ἀβροτόνου δὲ καὶ ὑσσώπου καὶ
ἴριδος τῆς ῥυπαρᾶς· ἔτι δὲ γεντιανῆς τὸ τετραπλάσιον·
pass_a_gloss: Pros hypozygion-phthora. Soldier-obstacle: nosesas-hippos, and war-oplophoron pack-beast, and needed-things-carrying nōtophoros-oreus. To-all these the of-other-and-loimic-pathe therapeia thus to-be-brought. [Nosounton-ktenon therapeia.] Selinon-seed hemixesta three; linseed epitriton; tēlis double the-second; ground-orobos quadruple the-tēlis; these metron-wise. Panakes-root and Illyrian-iris and Sabine-brathy, ana 48 drachmai; and of the-three-together tetraplasion, old unsalted axungion-weight. Each of the-said dry things idiai chopped and sieved, with old-oinos and the-stear palynetai, then into artiskoi reshaped, in-skia dried. At chreia, royal-karyon-size (seven grammata it-draws) with honey-kyathoi three is-pounded, then in oldest-and-spoudaiotatos oinos dissolved; xestes one let-it-be; three-days each-year the-ktēnos taking-in will-not suffer the-thanatēsion ktenōn-pathos. To the-nosountes, anti-oinos, hydati dissolved of those who-introduced the-equal before. If pithyē/bran even from nosera-systasis necessity become to-use, artiskoi-absence, three kollurai wine-soaked enchymatizein, the-way many send-in axungion kath' hauto. Those-by-whom lykoi are-hunted rhaista, they thus iōntai the-said pathe of hypozygia: lykos-kreas broad-schelides, lean they-dry hanging over-kapnos, such-as we of-boves. At chreia one-must-hepsein some of-these until it-syntakē, and to-the-hydōr ana hemixeston of-oinos and-elaion mixing, each-year enchymatizein. Also of a-nekros-already-sēsēpōs kyōn the-head apotmētheisa loosens that-deinon pathos for the-nosōn hippos; he by the-odmē-apophora continuous smoked will-be-healed. [Poikilōtera polyhylōtera synthesis.] The-polyhylōtaton, of-which I myself had-peira, which leading Rhōmaioi chrōntai, mathein anankaion: eight-drachmai amōmon-botryitēs and each-peperis, black and white <lacuna> the-double; triple phyllon and pyrethron and aristolochia, abronoton and hyssōpos and rhypara-iris; still gentianē tetraplasion.
pass_b_english: For the destruction of pack-animals. A horse that has fallen sick is a hindrance to a soldier, and so is a pack-animal carrying arms in war, and a pack-mule carrying the necessaries. To all these such a treatment of both the other affections and the plague-affections must be brought.

Treatment of sick cattle. Three half-xestai of celery seed; and four-thirds as much linseed; of fenugreek, double the second; of ground vetch, quadruple the fenugreek: these by measure. Of allheal-root and of Illyrian iris and of savin of the Sabine grass, forty-eight drachmas each; and quadruple the three together, the weight of old unsalted axle-grease. Each of the dry things named is chopped separately and sieved, and is dusted with old wine and the fat; then, shaped into little cakes, it is dried in the shade. At need, as much as a royal walnut's size (which weighs seven grammata) is pounded with three kyathoi of honey, then dissolved in the oldest and most serious wine; let it be one xestes. Taking it in for three days of each year, the beast will not suffer the killing affection of cattle. For the sick, instead of the wine, it is dissolved in water, of those who introduced the equal before.

If need should arise to use bran also, even from the sick constitution, in the absence of the cakes, drench three rolls soaking them in wine, the way many insert axle-grease by itself. Those for whom wolves are hunted most easily heal the pack-animals of the affections named thus: cutting broad thin steaks of wolf-flesh, they dry them lean, hanging them over smoke, such as we do of cattle. At need one must boil some of these until it melts, and mixing with the water a half-xestes each of wine and of oil, drench each year. A head cut off from a dog already dead and rotten also loosens that terrible affection for the sick horse; smoked by the continuous exhalation of the smell, he will be healed.

A more various and more many-ingredient composition. The most many-ingredient, of which I myself had trial, which the leading Romans use, it is necessary to learn: as much as eight drachmas of cluster-amomum and of each pepper, black and white — [lacuna] the double; triple of leaf and of pyrethrum and of aristolochia, and of wormwood and of hyssop and of the dirty iris; and still of gentian the quadruple.

choices.why: πρὸς here matches the pinax remedy-titles (for a wound, for a kicking mule): against the destruction, i.e. to keep the beasts from dying. The body is therapy, not a poison for the train.
rejected: toward the ruin of mules as a weapon
